item.title: The Fall of the New Epstein
item.description: An expose of Jared Kushner’s ties to MBS and MBZ will trigger a House investigation when the Democrats take Congress. Trump has his popcorn ready.
item.dc:creator: Predictive History
item.content:encoded:
Matthew Cole, a national security investigative journalist, has published an excerpt from his new book in Vanity Fair which alleges that Jared Kushner has access to a $2 billion slush fund to facilitate his Middle East policy (which somehow entailed paying for the services of a warlord, a mercenary, and a hitman). The fund was set up by the United Arab Emirates’ Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan (MBZ) and Saudi Arabia’s Mohammed bin Salman (MBS).

Because this is a national security story, it’s convoluted. Apparently, the Dutch (considered the Sixth member of the Five Eyes countries) hacked into a Russia database that had screenshots of Kushner’s iPhone communications. The Dutch reverse-engineered the Russian hack, and by early 2018 could see everything on Kushner’s screen. Hoping to find evidence of collusion with Russia, the Dutch instead found that Kushner had an alliance of mutual political convenience with MBZ and MBS, who provided a $2 billion slush fund for Kushner to circumvent Congressional oversight:

“Kushner, UAE ruler Mohamed bin Zayed (MBZ) and Mohammed bin Salman (MBS) of Saudi Arabia, converged at an auspicious moment. MBS wanted to be crown prince. MBZ wanted to blow up Obama’s Iran nuclear deal, and Kushner wanted both to help him force the Palestinians into a deal that Israel would accept.

Early in the first Trump administration, MBZ and MBS offered to pay for a slush fund dedicated to helping the new administration with foreign policy goals. The idea was to help pay for Trump’s promised wall between Mexico and the US, for example, in an effort to secure a second term in the White House.”

We’ve always known that Jared Kushner was close to MBS, who overruled his auditors and personally pushed for a $2 billion investment into Kushner’s private equity fund in 2021. But this book excerpt offers a clear paper trail, and reveals how Kushner operated his slush fund. The excerpt also alleges that Kushner was working as an agent of a foreign government:

“Although Kushner’s position as senior advisor to the president was unpaid, he was an official government employee. Not only did his position require financial disclosures for ethics regulations, but each year he worked in the White House, he had to file both a public and confidential financial form, known as the Executive Branch Personnel Public Financial Disclosure Report, also known as a 278e disclosure. Because he had access to classified government secrets, Kushner was required to disclose any bank account to which he had signatory—or beneficiary—access.

Kushner’s apparent betrayal of the public trust, however, went further than his failure to disclose the secret Alpha account in the UAE or the Beta account in Israel. By giving him access to roughly $2 billion, regardless of how the money was used, MBZ and MBS were paying for his influence within the US government. Any efforts he made to shape US policy that came from a foreign government that had provided him with money would make him an agent of a foreign power. US law requires citizens who lobby on behalf of a foreign power to declare themselves and the country they are working on behalf of to the Justice Department.”

Violation of the Foreign Agents Registration Act (FARA) is very serious in Washington. But because Washington is Washington it’s also common. It’s the elite equivalent of lying on your mortgage loan, and a few of Trump’s closest advisors have been charged with this:

  • Paul Manafort, who advised Trump’s 2016 election campaign, pleaded guilty to working on behalf of Ukraine. Trump subsequently pardoned him.

  • General Michael Flynn, who was Trump’s first National Security Advisor, pleaded guilty to lying on his 2017 FARA application, in which he retroactively registered as an agent for Turkey. Trump subsequently pardoned him.

  • The billionaire and Trump advisor Tom Barrack was charged in 2021, but was acquitted of acting as an unregistered agent of the UAE. He currently serves as the ambassador to Turkey, and the Presidential Envoy to Iraq and Syria.

Trump and his allies have argued that these are political witch-hunts, and that is a valid argument. Trump’s own Department of Justice authorized former FBI director Robert Mueller and his team to investigate Russian interference in the 2016 election (“Russiagate”).

It’s common law enforcement practice to cast a wide net, and charge small fish to catch larger fish. Mueller subpoenaed Manafort and Flynn as part of his investigation, and their testimony proved to be self-incriminating. But they refused to implicate Trump, and/or Trump could not be implicated.

If the Democrats sweep Congress (as everyone expects), they will immediately investigate Kushner’s $2 billion slush fund. They hope that an investigation will net them their real target, but having been mentored by Roy Cohn Trump has learned how to steal, cheat, and lie without breaking the law. In Trump’s first impeachment trial, the Democrats charged him with “abuse of power” for threatening to withhold military aid to Ukraine if it did not offer political dirt on Joe Biden. That’s definitely wrong — but was it illegal?

item.title: The October Surprise
item.description: With a Blue Tsunami coming in November, many Democrats fear an October Surprise that could de-rail the mid-term elections. The real surprise is that Trump wants the Democrats to control Congress.
item.dc:creator: Predictive History
item.content:encoded:
Both polls and prediction markets have the Democrats sweeping Congress in November. It is almost certain that the Democrats will take the House of Representatives, and now it seems likely that the Democrats will win the Senate. In battleground Michigan, Democrat Abdul Al-Sayed is poised to become the first Muslim in the Senate. Even previously safe red states are being contested. In the Kansas senate race, Democrat Adam Hamilton has a slim lead over incumbent senator Roger Marshall. If the polls are correct and James Talarico triumphs in the Texas senatorial race, he would be the first Democrat to win a state-wide office in thirty years.

Currently, with less than three weeks to go before the mid-terms, prediction markets give the Democrats a 75 percent chance of sweeping Congress. A year ago, the same prediction markets gave the Republicans a 73 percent of keeping the Senate.

Democrats and Republicans can agree on why the mid-terms are trending blue. President Donald Trump’s favorability rating is in the low thirties, which is mostly due to his unprovoked war against Iran and the ensuing cost of living crisis. Not helping matters is Trump’s indifference:

  • On May 12, 2026 when a reporter asked Trump if domestic economic concerns would impact his negotiations with Iran, he replied: “I don’t think about Americans’ financial situation. Not even a little bit. The only thing that matters when I’m talking about Iran, they can’t have a nuclear weapon.”

  • On May 27, Trump told reporters he did not care about the mid-terms while at a Cabinet meeting discussing the Iran War and nuclear negotiations.

  • On June 10, Trump was asked about inflation due to the Iran War, and he responded: “I love inflation.”

Trump seems to be waking up to the calamity ahead of him. He is aggressively campaigning across the country, promising five thousand dollars to every adult American if the Republicans win the mid-terms.

The Democrats cannot seem to believe how Trump has just handed them the mid-terms, and so they’re war-gaming an October Surprise. Will AI videos of election fraud allow Trump to deploy ICE to “safeguard” elections in November? Will a domestic mass casualty event allow Trump to suspend elections? After the Blue Tsunami, will Trump cry “election fraud” and contest the results?

How realistic are these fears?

Trump has been trying to create pretexts to meddle in state elections, but neither the Supreme Court nor Congress has played along. Last week, the Supreme Court in a 6-3 ruling allowed the Trump administration to prosecute state officials who issue mail-in ballots to ineligible voters. But the Supreme Court did not address whether Trump has the authority to demand that state officials first prove voters are eligible before issuing mail-in ballots — which practically means that Trump does not. Congress has yet to pass the Safeguard American Voter Eligibility Act (SAVE America Act), which would have required voters to provide proof of identity at the ballot box.

Without a legal and legislative foundation, it would be hard for Trump to deny the inevitability of a Democratically-controlled Congress. Once in power, the Democrats will investigate and subpoena White House staffers, revealing to the public the corruption and ineptitude of the Trump White House. The biggest surprise for the Democrats will be that Trump would not mind that outcome.

item.title: The Mad Folly of the Saudi Crown Prince
item.description: MbS is determined to destroy the Houthis. The Middle East will burn, and the only winner will be Israel.
item.dc:creator: Predictive History
item.content:encoded:
As of this writing, the Houthis have struck Terminal 3 of King Khalid International Airport, forcing authorities to evacuate the airport. There is fear that this is a mass casualty event, and fifty ambulances have rushed to the scene.

Earlier this week, on Wednesday, Saudi authorities reported that a Houthi strike on the same airport killed three Saudi civilians, including a pilot. The Houthis have imposed both an aerial and naval blockade on the Saudis. They have attacked four major Saudi airports, and they have launched a ballistic missile against Saudi Arabia’s Ghawar field, the world’s largest oilfield. The Houthis are intending to cripple the Saudi Arabian economy to force a surrender. Saudi oil production is the lowest since 1990, and its production has fallen by at least a third since the start of the Iran conflict.

The Saudis have been in this position before. In the Yemeni civil war, the Saudis and their allies besieged the Houthis, and the United Nations reported that over 100,000 died in the ensuing famine. The UK-based NGO Save the Children estimated that 85,000 children under the age of five died because of the civil war.

The Houthis would not submit, and their attacks on Saudi oilfields forced the Saudis to seek peace terms on April 1, 2022. With the current strain on the Saudi economy, analysts are expecting the Saudi crown prince Mohammad bin Salman (MbS) to negotiate a peace. How could Saudi Arabia possibly hope to triumph when its oilfields, airports, and pipelines are so vulnerable to Houthi drones and ballistic missiles?

Unfortunately, the crown prince believes that now is the best opportunity to end the Houthi threat once and for all, and turn Saudi Arabia into a regional power.

item.title: All-In on AI
item.description: Why the Anthropic IPO might burst the AI bubble, and why that might be the plan.
item.dc:creator: Predictive History
item.content:encoded:
I was tempted to make a bet on Polymarket that Anthropic will not have an initial public offering (IPO) before the end of year. Currently, there is an 83 percent probability that Anthropic does have one before the year ends.

It is attempting to raise $100 billion dollars, giving it a two trillion dollar valuation. But it has only $4.6 billion in 2025 revenue (with a net operating loss of $42 billion), and $518 billion in commitments. And the war in the Middle East means that the crazy rich Arabs and Asians aren’t as crazy and as rich.

To distract from its dismal financials, Anthropic has resorted to fear-mongering to drum up investor interest. In its IPO prospectus, the company warns that its AI models could pose “catastrophic or existentialist risks to humanity.” Risk factors occupy 80 of 261 pages, and the prospectus claims that AI models could attempt to blackmail, deceive, and manipulate humans to avoid being shut down. This implies that in the long-term AI models may seek to dominate, and enslave or eliminate humans.

Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei has published an essay calling for more guardrails on AI development. Anthropic has spent months consulting with religious scholars on how to make its chatbot Claude more “moral.” Unfortunately, Amodei has yet to tell investors how he plans to turn a profit.

AI doom porn is dominating social media. The computer scientist Nate Soares is going on podcasts, warning AI may doom us all. I tried to understand his reasoning, but his conversations can be broken down like this:

Host: “Tell us how AI will eventually outsmart, and kill us all.”

Soares: “I can’t do that because AI will be so much smarter than us.”

The main source of public concern is the July 2026 Hugging Face incident, in which openAI’s autonomous AI agents launched an unauthorized attack against the Hugging Face platform. It seems that the neural network algorithms underlying AI are so complex that researchers cannot imagine how these agents will actually behave in real life.

This has always been a problem in AI research. For example, in order to get a perfect score, an AI pilot would crash the plane during a flight simulation in order to overload the system. This happened even though the AI pilot was instructed never to intentionally crash the plane. The problem is that the AI was also programmed to prioritize results over compliance. In other words, AI cheats because humans reward cheating.

And because private companies that prioritize profit especially reward cheating, governments may be forced to nationalize AI. And that’s exactly what these private companies are betting on.

Let me explain.

item.title: Chinese Whispers
item.description: A week before the Trump-Xi Washington summit, rumors about domestic political turmoil are leaking out of China. That’s worrying for Trump and Xi.
item.dc:creator: Predictive History
item.content:encoded:
Next Wednesday, President Xi Jinping arrives in Washington DC for a three-day visit. This will be the second of four scheduled meetings between President Xi and President Trump this year, as the two attempt to move away from a relationship of “strategic competition” to “strategic stability.”

Xi’s visit comes at a time when China is finding itself in crisis. Chinese consumers refuse to spend money, flooding has wreaked havoc across the country, and China begins mass mobilization to prepare for war against a rapidly re-militarizing Japan.

Not helping matters is how this past week alone three major rumors have dominated the Chinese-language Internet. They are (in order of credibility):

  • Huawei’s Founder Ren Zhengfei has fled China. Huawei leaked military secrets, and Chinese authorities sought to arrest Huawei’s first family.

  • President Xi Jinping’s health is failing. He had a medical emergency in India where he was attending the BRICS summit hosted by Modi. He flew back to China, and was hospitalized. Most believe that the emergency was minor, but there are some who believed he suffered a mini-stroke.

  • Bo Xilai has escaped prison. He is President Xi’s more charismatic and even more ambitious political rival, and he has been imprisoned since 2013 after failing to seize power in a coup d’etat. He is currently the only one capable of stealing the throne from Xi, and he has found refuge in southwest China, where the military divisions stationed there are in open defiance of Beijing.

These rumors come at a sensitive time in Chinese politics, and the next year may define China’s next twenty years. Next autumn, the Chinese Communist Party will convene the 21st National Congress to decide its top leadership, and Xi wants to secure a fourth term. That is perhaps why these rumors are not just allowed to spread – they’re also being amplified across the Chinese-language Internet and beyond.

item.title: The Houthis On the March
item.description: A Saudi offensive against the Houthis would doom the United States’ war effort in the Middle East.
item.dc:creator: Predictive History
item.content:encoded:
In December 2024, Hay’at Tahrir al-Sham (HTS) in their pick-up trucks launched a probing attack against the Assad government in Syria. To everyone’s surprise, a 170,000-strong army that had weathered 14 years of civil war suddenly withered into the desert wind. Bashar al-Assad, a London-trained ophthalmologist who inherited his father’s brutal dictatorship, fled to Moscow, and the HTS leader Ahmed Al-Sharaa, an internationally-sanctioned terrorist, picked up the crown.

The Assad government’s sudden collapse was a devastating blow to the Axis of Resistance. Iran could no longer use the Syrian land bridge to supply Hezbollah, and Israel now had the Syrian air bridge to strike Tehran. Eighteen months later, Israel launched Operation Rising Lion, and initiated the 12-day War.

And the rest is history. If Syria had not fallen, there would still be a precarious peace in the Middle East today.

With Ansar Allah’s recent push towards the Yemeni coast, we may experience a similar inflection point.

Ansar Allah (more commonly referred to as the Houthis) have been at war since 2014. Yemen is an unwieldy Hodge-podge of tribes, and the insurgent Houthis fought against the government of Abdrabbuh Mansur Hadi, who called upon his patron Saudi Arabia to intervene. The Houthis are Shia Muslims, and Iran’s Middle East envoy Qassem Soleimani (who would later be assassinated in a drone strike ordered by Trump on January 3rd, 2020) cultivated them as a counter to Saudi Arabia, which was Iran’s main regional rival.

Hoping to emulate the United States’ successful 1991 “Desert Storm” campaign to dislodge the Iraqis from Kuwait, the Saudis initially committed 150,000 troops and 100 warplanes against the Houthis in operation “Decisive Storm.”

The Saudis also organized a broad coalition. The United Arab Emirates, Egypt, Sudan, Jordan, Morocco, Kuwait, Qatar, and Bahrain all provided direct military support. The United States, the United Kingdom, and France provided arms, intelligence, and targeting to the coalition.

After spending tens of billions of dollars without effect, Saudi Arabia was forced to sign an UN-brokered truce in 2022. The fanatical Houthis could not be starved into submission, and while the Saudi coalition could never penetrate into the Houthi mountains the Houthis could easily burn down the Saudi energy infrastructure with their Iran-supplied drones and ballistic missiles. The Saudis learned the hard way that the Houthis could never be defeated as long as Iran was still standing. (This was a reason why Saudi Arabia urged Trump to start his war against Iran.)

The United States would also learn the tenacity of the Houthis. In response to the Gaza genocide, the Houthis disrupted Red Sea shipping. President Joe Biden organized a twenty-nation campaign called Operation Prosperity Guardian on December 18, 2023 to counter the Houthi disruption. The campaign was a failure from the start, and on May 6, 2025 President Donald Trump ordered a unilateral withdrawal.

The Houthis did not join the war when the United States and Israel first bombarded Iran on February 28 of this year. Saudi Arabia and the Houthis had a precarious peace, and on July 13th Saudi Arabia launched an air-strike on Houthi-held Sanaa International Airport, supposedly to prevent an Iranian plane from landing. In retaliation, the Houthis resumed threatening Saudi shipping in the Red Sea. On August 7th, Saudi Arabia signed a mutual defense pact called the Mecca Accords with Turkey and Pakistan.

This defense pact is already being tested. This week, in a probing attack, the Houthis surprised everyone, probably including themselves, by spreading far and wide, as Saudi-backed Yemeni government forces withered into the desert wind. This Thursday, the Houthis captured Mokha, a vital Red Sea port. Then they captured Perim, a strategic island that cements the Houthi control over the strategic Bab El-Mandeb Strait. The Houthis now control Yemen’s Red Sea coastline, and together with Iran they dictate the flow of 30 percent of the world’s energy.

item.title: Spy Versus Spy
item.description: John Ratcliffe visits Russia, as Putin prepares for war against NATO.
item.dc:creator: Predictive History
item.content:encoded:
In the 1975 movie “Dog Day Afternoon,” Sonny Wortzik (played by Al Pacino) and Salvatore “Sal” Naturile (played by John Cazale) hold up a bank, take hostages, and demand to flee in a private plane. FBI Special Agent Sheldon (played by James Broderick) arrives at the scene, and asks to check up on the well-being of the hostages. He is there not to see the hostages, but to size up the two bank robbers.

By studying the anxiety in their faces, Sheldon determines that Sonny cannot kill, but Sal will. “We’ll take care of Sal,” Sheldon whispers to Sonny, who replies without conviction that he’ll never betray his friend.

The FBI agrees to all terms, and sends a car and driver. Sonny calls out the driver as a plant, causing immediate dismay and consternation among the FBI agents. Sonny is just too smart for them. He singles out the biggest nerd among the FBI agents, and designates him as their driver, unwittingly co-operating in his own doom. During the bumpy ride, the FBI “nerd” pulls out a gun from a hidden compartment, and shoots Sal in the head.

A long time ago, I used to play a lot of Texas Hold’em poker, and I would observe opponents staring down each other to figure out each other’s hole cards. It took some time before I realized that they just weren’t interested in the hole cards. They were sizing each other out, and planning for the future. The best players would make an obvious bluff or let one slide to trick their opponent into making a riskier, more costly play in the future. All of this was subconscious and intuitive, invisible to even themselves.

This Tuesday, John Ratcliffe, Trump’s CIA Director, secretly visited Moscow for a few hours to meet with his Russian counterparts, and he may or may not have met with Putin. The Wall Street Journal reported that he was there to warn the Russians against further aggression, and Trump himself downplayed the visit as “semi-routine.”

The last time a CIA director visited Moscow was in November 2021 when William Burns went uninvited to warn against an invasion of Ukraine. Burns threatened dire retaliation, and Putin (having sized up Biden accurately) went ahead with the invasion three months later. So Ratcliffe’s visit is significant, and one mystery is whether he met with Putin.

There are some analysts who see Ratcliffe as a war hawk, and his intelligence assessment that Iran was close to developing a nuclear weapon was a major reason why Trump went to war against Iran. Director of National Intelligence Tulsi Gabbard (who argued against this assessment) clashed repeatedly with Ratcliffe.

With her resignation the war hawks within the Trump administration seem ascendant, but Ratcliffe got to where he is because he has demonstrated intense personal loyalty to Trump. As a Congressman, he attacked Mueller’s investigation into Trump’s Russia ties, and was Trump’s main champion during the impeaching hearings in Congress. As director of national intelligence in Trump’s first term and as director of the CIA in his second, Ratcliffe released classified documents that favored Trump politically. Ratcliffe won out in his clash with Gabbard because Trump trusted him in a way that he could not trust her.

This suggests that Ratcliffe went to Russia as Trump’s emissary to deliver a message that could only be delivered in person. If he had gone to Russia to set red lines (as most reporting suggests) then this could have done through diplomatic channels – or he could have just given a press conference.

I understand that both the Russians and the Americans denied Ratcliffe met with Putin – but game theory suggests they had to meet. What then was the message that Trump wanted delivered to Putin personally?
